messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: int vectors
parts:
On 9/22/12 3:34 AM, Daniel Lee wrote:

> I'm going to have to extend the parser to allow for int vector types,
> but that shouldn't be a problem.

You mean a type that would translate to
Eigen's Matrix<int,Dynamic,1>?

What would it be used for?

Totally doable, of course. It would require
adding the new base type and type inference
rules to ast.hpp. And new I/O routines everywhere.

Int types are a bit simpler in that there's
no transform needed for inits or reverse transform
needed for parameters.

We'd talked about having something like

vector<basetype=int>

vector<basetype=real> == vector<> == vector

The other alternative would be to introduce
types int_vector, int_row_vector, int_matrix
and leave vector, row_vector and matrix as is.

- Bob

typename return_type<T_prob>::type

I haven't thought about how to generalize to multidimensional matrices
and 2d arrays yet. Can we define a consistent behavior for the
distributions? I'm guessing that you want:

matrix ~ normal(scalar, scalar)

to mean that each element in the matrix should be treated as y in the
distribution. That makes sense, but then what should be the
appropriate behaviors for things like:
matrix ~ normal(matrix, vector)
or
matrix ~ normal(vector, row_vector)
or
matrix[3,2] ~ normal(matrix[3,1], matrix[1,2]) (where dim is in the
square brackets)

If we can define consistent behavior, we can try to beef up the
VectorView stuff to do what we want. I really haven't thought about
these things too much, so maybe there's a simple answer to all of
this.

The 3 vector could be interpreted as applying to both columns and the 6 vector as applying sequentially to the six matrix entries. But if that is hard, then don't worry about it. It is not too much to ask users to make the input match or be scalars.

That makes sense, but then what should be the
appropriate behaviors for things like:
matrix ~ normal(matrix, vector)
or
matrix ~ normal(vector, row_vector)
or

I would say throw exception unless everything is the same size or is a scalar.
 
matrix[3,2] ~ normal(matrix[3,1], matrix[1,2]) (where dim is in the
square brackets)

I would have guessed that that was already legal, but if not it should be.
 

We don't allow the lhs, but this is currently illegal. The lengths of the parameters do not match. One is length 3 and the other is length 2.
Incompatible lengths should definitely result in a fatal exception. I mistakenly thought the above was a weird way to say scalar ~ normal(scalar, scalar).

If we can define consistent behavior, we can try to beef up the
VectorView stuff to do what we want. I really haven't thought about
these things too much, so maybe there's a simple answer to all of
this.

I don't think there is a simple answer for the

multidimensional ~ normal(multidimensional, multidimensional)

case unless all the multidimensional objects are the same dimension. R recycles and throws a warning if recycling doesn't come out right, but I think Stan should only recycle scalars.
 

What does "recycling" mean?

Recycling means repeating the elements of a vector until they match the length of a longer vector. In other words, this is technically legal in R

> set.seed(12345)
> rnorm(6, mean = 0:2, sd = 4:5) # implicit recycling
[1]  2.342115  4.547330  1.562787 -2.267486  3.423550 -7.089780
> set.seed(12345)
> rnorm(6, mean = c(0:2, 0:2), sd = c(4:5, 4:5, 4:5)) # explicit recycling
[1]  2.342115  4.547330  1.562787 -2.267486  3.423550 -7.089780

where the colon means a sequence of integers from the left to the right. But I think implicit recycling is too dangerous for Stan, except recycling scalars to match the length of a vector / matrix / array.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: Vectorized distributions
parts:
Option 0. The way I would think about this is in terms
of coercing the various inputs to sequences,
throwing an exception if they don't match in
sequence size, and repeating the function as many times
as they do.

scalar -- recycle to max length
std::vector -- natural sequence
Eigen column vec -- natural sequence
Eigen row vec -- natural sequence

This is what we have now

Option 1. Extend this in the obvious way to matrices:

Eigen matrix -- column major order

This would match what we do now and also match how
Eigen defines operator()(int) for matrices.

If we do add them, I think it'll be simplest to just
define the natural sequentialization and allow
anything with matching sequence size. This matches
Eigen's unary operator()(int) behavior.

I agree that recycling is a bad idea for anything
other than a scalar. The only case I see it working
is recycling a row or column vector up to a matrix.
Or subarrays up to full arrays, like allowing
a CxD array to recycle up to an AxBxCxD array.
But that's starting to get awfully subtle.

Option 2. The only other thing that seems simple is to require
all the types to match other than scalar. But I
think everyone wants to allow 1D arrays, vectors
and row vectors to mix.

The major downside of this proposal is that you
could put in a 3 x 2 and a 2 x 3 matrix, and they'd
get converted to sequences as follows:

a[1,1], a[2,1], a[3,1], a[2,1], a[2,2], a[3,2]

b[1,1], b[2,1], b[1,2], b[2,2], b[1,3], b[2,3]

I can't imagine anywhere a user would do this and
it wouldn't be an error.

Option 3. The in between spec would be to require the sizes
to all match, and if there are matrices and/or arrays,
their dimensions all have to match.

I'm OK with any of these options, including not extending
to matrices.

Also, what about 2D, 3D or greater arrays?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Vectorized distributions
parts:
On Saturday, October 13, 2012 8:11:52 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Option 3.  The in between spec would be to require the sizes
to all match, and if there are matrices and/or arrays,
their dimensions all have to match.

I think I would be in favor of option 3. Almost anything should be allowed on the LHS, scalars should always be allowed on the RHS, but if a parameter on the RHS is not a scalar, it should match the dimensionality of the LHS and not just the size.

Ben

I think what's allowed on the left and right
should be symmetric (not yet considering when
there are multivariate quantities on the left
or right).

So this would mean:

OK: normal(matrix[m,n], real, real)
normal(real, matrix[m,n], real) (*)
normal(real, real, matrix[m,n])

BAD: normal(matrix[m,n], vector[m*n], real)
normal(matrix[m,n], matrix[n,m], real)

OK: normal(matrix[m,n], matrix[m,n], real);
normal(matrix[m,n], matrix[m,n], matrix[m,n]);

etc.

I understand that it's not going to be likely to see
the case (*) above, but I think it's easier to
keep all the implementations allowing it.

What about arrays?

??: normal(real[m,n], matrix[m,n], real)

- Bob
